chunks: And as for the right of your father, it is that you know that he is your root, and that without him you would not have been. So whatever you see in yourself that pleases you, know that your father is the root of the blessing upon you in it, and praise God and thank Him to the extent of that, and there is no strength except with God.

key_terms.وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللَّهِ: and there is no strength except with God

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and ethical right of one's father according to Shia tradition?
ai.summary: Imam Zayn al-Abidin frames the father as the 'root' (asl' of the self, establishing a metaphysical link between paternal lineage and personal virtue. This perspective encourages believers to view their own admirable qualities as divine blessings mediated through the father, thereby transforming familial gratitude into worship. The narration concludes by grounding this appreciation in the Shia spiritual practice of acknowledging divine power through 'La quwwata illa billah'.
